subproblems.title: A Borel countably n-rectifiable set is, up to a null set, a disjoint union of bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and countably n-rectifiable. Then there are Lipschitz maps F_i : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, Borel sets B_i ⊆ ℝ^n and constants m_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| for a, a' ∈ B_i, F_i is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B_i, each F_i(B_i) is a Borel subset of M, the sets F_i(B_i) are pairwise disjoint, and H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet M → CountablyRectifiable n M → ∃ (F : ℕ → Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (m : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ i, ∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L (F i)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) ∧ (∀ i, 0 < m i) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, ∀ a' ∈ B i, m i * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F i a - F i a'‖) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, DifferentiableAt ℝ (F i) a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ (F i) a)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (F i '' B i)) ∧ (∀ i, F i '' B i ⊆ M) ∧ Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (F i '' B i) (F j '' B j)) ∧ μHE[n] (M \ ⋃ i, F i '' B i) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted DAG declaration dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.bilipschitz_pieces-a1, candidate commit a2ba78fca36b5fe8a0051278d30da09823c8b59c); its frozen Lean type is reused byte-for-byte, so no new worker is provisioned. Role in this decomposition: it is the measurable-piece version (a)–(f) of step 2 of the parent proof, applied by the parent to M₁ = M ∩ K; the parent's step 2(g) (compact inner regularity) is not needed because every later use (area formula, Lusin–Souslin, piece_tangent, piece_pullback) only requires Borel pieces. The audited proof of that declaration follows; inside it, 'the parent proof' and 'sibling' refer to that declaration's own original parent node and siblings, not to this decomposition.
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (with the n = 0 provisions of its step 10). It plays the role of Simon's decomposition of Lemma 1.2 / Remark 1.3 of Ch. 3 (chapter-03.txt lines 25–75: M = ⋃_j M_j disjoint, M_j ⊆ N_j, H^n(M_0) = 0), with bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces in place of pieces of C¹ submanifolds; families are indexed by ℕ and empty pieces are allowed. Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] (on ℝ^n it equals Lebesgue measure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. Rectifiable cover. By CountablyRectifiable n M there are M₀ ⊆ E with H^n(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^n → E (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n).
2. Regular sets. Let G_j := {a ∈ ℝ^n : F_j is differentiable at a and DF_j(a) is injective} (SimonGMT areaRegularSet F_j). G_j is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_areaRegularSet) and H^n(F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero with s = univ; finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n).
3. Coercivity constant and radius. For an injective linear A : ℝ^n → E choose m(A) > 0 with (†) |Ah| ≥ m(A)|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^n: if n ≥ 1 take m(A) := min{|Ah| : |h| = 1} (the unit sphere is compact and nonempty and h ↦ |Ah| is continuous and positive on it; for h ≠ 0 apply this to h/|h|; h = 0 is trivial); if n = 0 take m(A) := 1 (the only vector is h = 0). (Alternatively m(A) := 1/K for K > 0 with AntilipschitzWith K A from Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith, valid in every dimension.) Define r : (ℝ^n →L[ℝ] E) → ℝ≥0 by r(A) := m(A)/2 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise. Then r(A) ≠ 0 for every A.
4. Partition. For each j apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to f := F_j, s := G_j, f' := fderiv ℝ F_j (for a ∈ G_j, F_j is differentiable at a, so HasFDerivWithinAt F_j (DF_j(a)) G_j a) and the radius r of step 3 (rpos holds). It gives pairwise disjoint measurable sets t_{j,k} ⊆ ℝ^n (k ∈ ℕ) with G_j ⊆ ⋃_k t_{j,k}, and continuous linear maps A_{j,k} with ApproximatesLinearOn F_j A_{j,k} (G_j ∩ t_{j,k}) (r(A_{j,k})), i.e. |F_j(a) − F_j(a') − A_{j,k}(a − a')| ≤ r(A_{j,k})|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ G_j ∩ t_{j,k}; and if G_j ≠ ∅ then A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) for some y ∈ G_j.
5. Bi-Lipschitz pieces. Put D_{j,k} := G_j ∩ t_{j,k} (Borel) and ρ_{j,k} := r(A_{j,k}) > 0. Claim: |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ ρ_{j,k}|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ D_{j,k}. If D_{j,k} = ∅ this is vacuous. Otherwise G_j ≠ ∅, so A := A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) with y ∈ G_j is injective and ρ_{j,k} = m(A)/2; by step 4 and (†), |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ |A(a − a')| − (m(A)/2)|a − a'| ≥ (m(A)/2)|a − a'|. In particular F_j is injective on D_{j,k}, and F_j is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of D_{j,k} ⊆ G_j.
6. Enumeration. Let i ↦ (j(i), k(i)) be the bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ (Nat.unpair). Put F_i := F_{j(i)}, D_i := D_{j(i),k(i)}, m_i := ρ_{j(i),k(i)} > 0, and N_i := F_i(D_i). F_i is continuous, D_i Borel and F_i injective on D_i, so N_i is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
7. Disjoint pieces. Define B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}). B_i is Borel (F_i continuous; M and the N_{i'} Borel) and F_i(B_i) = (N_i ∩ M) ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'} =: P_i, which is Borel and contained in M. Since B_i ⊆ D_i, the lower bound m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| and the differentiability/injectivity of DF_i hold on B_i, and F_i is Lipschitz. If i' < i then P_{i'} ⊆ N_{i'} and P_i ∩ N_{i'} = ∅, so the P_i are pairwise disjoint. (This is the parent's recursive definition B_i := (D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M)) ∖ F_i^{-1}(⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(B_{i'})) in closed form: by induction ⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(B_{i'}) = M ∩ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}.)
8. Null remainder. Let x ∈ M ∖ (M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)). By step 1, x = F_j(a) for some j and a, and a ∈ G_j. Then a ∈ t_{j,k} for some k, so a ∈ D_i for the index i with (j(i), k(i)) = (j, k), and x ∈ N_i ∩ M. If i₀ is the least index with x ∈ N_{i₀}, then x ∈ P_{i₀}. Hence M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j), a countable union of H^n-null sets (steps 1–2), so H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
9. n = 0 and n > P need no separate treatment: for n = 0 every A is injective, m(A) = 1, r(A) = 1/2, every map ℝ^0 → E is differentiable with injective derivative (G_j = ℝ^0), and each D_i ⊆ ℝ^0 has at most one point; for n > P no linear map ℝ^n → E is injective, so all G_j are empty, all B_i = ∅, and step 8 says H^n(M) = 0. (Imports: areaRegularSet and its lemmas live in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz, which the submission may import; the frozen statement does not use it.)
proof_key_steps: Cover M by M₀ ∪ ⋃F_j(ℝ^n) and remove the null images F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j) of the non-regular points.
Radius r(A) := m(A)/2 for injective A (m(A) a coercivity constant, 1 when n = 0), r(A) := 1 otherwise, so r(A) ≠ 0 for all A.
Mathlib's partition theorem gives pieces G_j ∩ t_{j,k} on which F_j is bi-Lipschitz with lower constant r(A_{j,k}).
Enumerate the pieces over ℕ; their images are Borel by Lusin–Souslin.
B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(D_{i'})) yields disjoint Borel images in M covering M up to a null set.

   - since ∫ Θ dμ < ∞, Θ < ∞ μ-a.e. (ae_lt_top), so (b_i(x))_i is summable for a.e. x (ENNReal.summable_toReal);

It is applied with Y = M (sibling orient_piece) and with Y = H(B) (sibling piece_imrep); hence the antecedent (TL) of the parent statement is not needed by the split. The audited proof of that declaration follows; inside it, 'the parent proof' and 'sibling' refer to that declaration's own original parent node and siblings, not to this decomposition.
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (density lemma). It is the bi-Lipschitz analogue of Simon's proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" of Ch. 3 (chapter-03.txt lines 109–143), which compares M with a C¹ manifold N_j and controls M ∖ N_j by the upper density theorem; here the C¹ piece is replaced by the bi-Lipschitz image F(B), the blow-up of F(B) is computed by the area formula, and the upper-density bound of the parent's step 5(i) is replaced by the elementary bi-Lipschitz estimate of step 3 below (a valid simplification: it uses only m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| on B). Definition used: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y y Q means finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{y,r}(Y)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0⁺ for every f ∈ C_c(E) (Simon Ch. 3 1.4, chapter-03.txt lines 77–85). Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] on E or on ℝ^n; λ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n (= μHE[n] there, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); A := F(B); B̄_r(z), B_r(z) closed and open balls; η_{y,r}(z) := r^{-1}(z − y) (= SimonGMT blowUpMap y r); J_F(a) := normDet(DF(a)) (= SimonGMT areaJacobianAt F a); L_b := DF(b); ω_n := λ(B̄_1(0)) ∈ (0, ∞); ‖f‖_∞ := sup|f|.
0. Preliminaries. (a) F is continuous and injective on B (m > 0), so A is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn), and A ⊆ Y ⊆ U. (b) The inverse G : A → B of F|_B satisfies |G(y) − G(y')| ≤ m^{-1}|y − y'|, so H^n(G(N)) ≤ m^{-n}H^n(N) for N ⊆ A (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le; μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with a constant c_n ∈ (0, ∞) depending only on n, Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). Hence if a property holds at every point of A outside an H^n-null set N, then it holds at F(b) for every b ∈ B ∖ G(N), and λ(G(N)) = 0. (c) Lipschitz images: H^n(F(S)) ≤ L^n H^n(S) = L^n λ(S) for S ⊆ ℝ^n (LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, same normalization). (d) Scaling: for r > 0, η_{y,r} is the homothety of ratio r^{-1} about y followed by the translation z ↦ z − y, so H^n(η_{y,r}(S)) = r^{-n}H^n(S) for all S ⊆ E (MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image, and invariance of μHE[n] under the isometry z ↦ z − y, Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image); η_{y,r} is a homeomorphism, so η_{y,r}(S) is Borel for Borel S. Hence for Borel S the image of H^n⌞S under the measurable embedding η_{y,r} is r^n·H^n⌞η_{y,r}(S), and ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} f dH^n = r^{-n}∫_S f(η_{y,r}(z)) dH^n(z) whenever either side is an integral of an integrable function (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, integral_smul_measure). (e) 0 ≤ J_F(a) ≤ L^n for every a, and J_F is Borel (SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt): ‖DF(a)‖ ≤ L (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; DF(a) = 0 where F is not differentiable), and normDet(T) ≤ ‖T‖^n for every linear T : ℝ^n → E, because normDet(T)·ω_n = H^n(T(B̄_1(0))) ≤ ‖T‖^n H^n(B̄_1(0)) = ‖T‖^n ω_n (Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and the Lipschitz image bound).
1. Countable compact cover. If U = ∅ then Y = ∅, so F(B) ⊆ ∅ forces B = ∅ and the claim is trivial (volume.restrict ∅ = 0); assume U ≠ ∅. U is open in the separable space E, so there are closed balls C_k = B̄_{s_k}(q_k) ⊆ U (k ∈ ℕ, s_k > 0) whose open balls B_{s_k}(q_k) cover U (centres in a countable dense set, positive rational radii, closures inside U). Each C_k is compact and ⊆ U, so H^n(Y ∩ C_k) < ∞.
2. Density of A in Y. Fix k and let ν_k := H^n⌞(Y ∩ C_k), a finite (hence locally finite) Borel measure (IsFiniteMeasure from H^n(Y ∩ C_k) < ∞, isFiniteMeasure_restrict). By the Besicovitch density theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div applied to ν_k and A; E is finite-dimensional), for ν_k⌞A-a.e. y: ν_k(A ∩ B̄_r(y))/ν_k(B̄_r(y)) → 1 as r → 0⁺. Since A ⊆ Y and A, Y, C_k are Borel, ν_k⌞A = H^n⌞(A ∩ C_k), so this holds for H^n-a.e. y ∈ A ∩ C_k. Discarding the countable union N₁ of the exceptional sets (H^n(N₁) = 0), every y ∈ A ∖ N₁ is density-good: the convergence holds for every k with y ∈ C_k.
3. Smallness of Y ∖ A. Let y = F(b) (b ∈ B) be density-good and choose k with y ∈ B_{s_k}(q_k); put r₀ := s_k − |y − q_k| > 0. For 0 < r < r₀, B̄_r(y) ⊆ C_k, so with a(r) := H^n(A ∩ B̄_r(y)) and z(r) := H^n((Y ∖ A) ∩ B̄_r(y)) we get ν_k(A ∩ B̄_r(y)) = a(r) and ν_k(B̄_r(y)) = a(r) + z(r) < ∞; by step 2, a(r)/(a(r) + z(r)) → 1, so for each ε ∈ (0, 1/2) there is r_ε ∈ (0, r₀) with z(r) ≤ ε(a(r) + z(r)), hence z(r) ≤ 2ε a(r), for 0 < r < r_ε. If a ∈ B and F(a) ∈ B̄_r(y) then m|a − b| ≤ |F(a) − F(b)| ≤ r, so A ∩ B̄_r(y) ⊆ F(B ∩ B̄_{r/m}(b)) and, by 0(c), a(r) ≤ L^n λ(B̄_{r/m}(b)) = L^n ω_n m^{-n} r^n (this bound holds for every b ∈ B and r > 0). Thus z(r) ≤ 2ε L^n ω_n m^{-n} r^n for r < r_ε, i.e. r^{-n} z(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺.
4. Good parameters. By Lebesgue's density and differentiation theorems for λ on ℝ^n (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for λ and B; IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for λ, an additive Haar measure, and J_F, which is bounded and Borel, hence locally integrable), λ-a.e. b ∈ B satisfies (α) b is a density point of B: λ(B̄_ρ(b) ∖ B)/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺, and (β) b is a Lebesgue point of J_F: ρ^{-n} ∫_{B̄_ρ(b)} |J_F(a) − J_F(b)| dλ(a) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺ (= ω_n times the average). Every b ∈ B with (α) also satisfies (γ) |L_b c| ≥ m|c| for all c ∈ ℝ^n. Proof of (γ): it is trivial for c = 0; let c ≠ 0 (so n ≥ 1). There are r_l → 0⁺ and c_l → c with b + r_l c_l ∈ B: otherwise there are ε ∈ (0, |c|) and r₁ > 0 with B ∩ (b + r B_ε(c)) = ∅ for all r ∈ (0, r₁); but b + r B_ε(c) ⊆ B̄_{r(|c|+ε)}(b) has measure r^n λ(B_ε(0)) = (ε/(|c|+ε))^n λ(B̄_{r(|c|+ε)}(b)) (open and closed balls have the same Lebesgue measure, Measure.addHaar_closedBall_eq_addHaar_ball, which needs ℝ^n nontrivial: true since c ≠ 0; λ scales by r^n under dilation by r), a fixed positive fraction of λ(B̄_ρ(b)) for every ρ = r(|c|+ε) < r₁(|c|+ε), contradicting (α). Then m r_l|c_l| ≤ |F(b + r_l c_l) − F(b)| = |r_l L_b c_l + o(r_l)| (differentiability at b, |c_l| bounded); divide by r_l and let l → ∞ to get m|c| ≤ |L_b c|.
5. Blow-up of A. Let b ∈ B satisfy (α) and (β), y := F(b), f ∈ C_c(E) and R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0). Put Φ_r(c) := (F(b + rc) − F(b))/r for r > 0, c ∈ ℝ^n.
 (a) Formula: η_{y,r}(A) ∩ B_R(0) = η_{y,r}(A ∩ B_{rR}(y)) has H^n-measure ≤ r^{-n} a(rR) ≤ L^n ω_n (R/m)^n < ∞ (0(d) and step 3's bound for a), so f is integrable on η_{y,r}(A). By 0(d), the weighted area formula for the injective Lipschitz map F on B (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn, finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n, applied to the weights (f∘η_{y,r})⁺ and (f∘η_{y,r})⁻ and subtracted; all terms are finite since f is bounded and only B ∩ B̄_{rR/m}(b) contributes) and the substitution a = b + rc (λ scales by r^n): ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n = r^{-n}∫_B J_F(a) f((F(a) − y)/r) dλ(a) = ∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(b + rc) J_F(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c).
 (b) Localisation: if b + rc ∈ B and f(Φ_r(c)) ≠ 0 then m r|c| ≤ |F(b + rc) − F(b)| < rR, so |c| < R/m; and by (γ), f(L_b c) = 0 for |c| ≥ R/m. So, with D := B̄_{R/m}(0) ⊆ ℝ^n, the integral in (a) is an integral over D, and I_∞ := ∫_{ℝ^n} J_F(b) f(L_b c) dλ(c) = ∫_D J_F(b) f(L_b c) dλ(c).
 (c) Convergence: for c ∈ D, |1_B(b + rc) J_F(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) − J_F(b) f(L_b c)| ≤ L^n‖f‖_∞ 1_{D ∖ r^{-1}(B − b)}(c) + ‖f‖_∞ |J_F(b + rc) − J_F(b)| + J_F(b)|f(Φ_r(c)) − f(L_b c)| (add and subtract J_F(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) and J_F(b) f(Φ_r(c)); 0(e)). Integrating over D: the first term gives L^n‖f‖_∞ r^{-n} λ(B̄_{rR/m}(b) ∖ B) → 0 by (α) (λ(B̄_{rR/m}(b)) = ω_n(R/m)^n r^n); the second gives ‖f‖_∞ r^{-n} ∫_{B̄_{rR/m}(b)} |J_F − J_F(b)| dλ → 0 by (β); the third is ≤ J_F(b) λ(D) sup_{c∈D} |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(L_b c)| → 0 because Φ_r → L_b uniformly on D (F is differentiable at b) and f is uniformly continuous. Hence ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n → I_∞ as r → 0⁺.
 (d) Identification: L_b is injective and linear with normDet(L_b) = J_F(b), and H^n(L_b(S)) = J_F(b) λ(S) for all S ⊆ ℝ^n (Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume). For Borel T ⊆ E, L_b(L_b^{-1}(T)) = range L_b ∩ T, so H^n(range L_b ∩ T) = J_F(b) λ(L_b^{-1}(T)), i.e. H^n⌞range L_b is the image measure of J_F(b)·λ under L_b; as an injective linear map between finite-dimensional spaces is a closed (hence measurable) embedding, MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map gives I_∞ = J_F(b)∫_{ℝ^n} f(L_b c) dλ(c) = ∫_{range L_b} f dH^n.
6. Conclusion. Let N₂ ⊆ B be the λ-null set of b ∈ B where (α) or (β) fails, and N₃ := G(N₁ ∩ A), λ-null by 0(b) and step 2. Let b ∈ B ∖ (N₂ ∪ N₃) (a (volume.restrict B)-conull set); then F(b) is density-good. Let y := F(b), f and R as in step 5, k and r₀ as in step 3. For 0 < r < r₀/R, B̄_{rR}(y) ⊆ C_k, so H^n(η_{y,r}(Y) ∩ B_R(0)) = r^{-n}H^n(Y ∩ B_{rR}(y)) ≤ r^{-n}H^n(Y ∩ C_k) < ∞ and f is integrable on η_{y,r}(Y); η_{y,r}(Y) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets η_{y,r}(A) and η_{y,r}(Y ∖ A), so |∫_{η_{y,r}(Y)} f dH^n − ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ H^n(η_{y,r}(Y ∖ A) ∩ B_R(0)) ≤ ‖f‖_∞ r^{-n} z(rR) = ‖f‖_∞ R^n (rR)^{-n} z(rR) → 0 by step 3. With step 5, ∫_{η_{y,r}(Y)} f dH^n → ∫_{range L_b} f dH^n as r → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0), for every f ∈ C_c(E). Since L_b is injective on ℝ^n, finrank(range L_b) = n. This is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y (F b) (range DF(b)), for (volume.restrict B)-a.e. b.
7. Dimension zero. The argument is valid for n = 0 as written: ℝ^0 = {0}, λ is the unit point mass, B ⊆ {0}, ω_0 = 1 and r^{±0} = 1, J_F ≡ 1 (normDet of a map out of ℝ^0, LinearMap.normDet_of_subsingleton), (γ) is vacuous, D = {0}, integrals over ℝ^0 are evaluations at 0, and range L_b = {0} has finrank 0. (Imports: the Lean proof needs Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz and Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaApproximation for the area formula and measurable_areaJacobianAt, and Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.NormDet; the submission may add these imports, the frozen statement does not use them.)

H^n(F(B) ∩ B̄_r(F b)) = O(r^n) by the bi-Lipschitz bound, hence H^n((Y ∖ F(B)) ∩ B̄_r(F b)) = o(r^n).
At density points of B that are Lebesgue points of J_F, |DF(b)c| ≥ m|c|, and the area formula plus rescaling give ∫_{η(F(B))} f → J_F(b)∫ f(DF(b)c) dc = ∫_{range DF(b)} f dH^n.

subproblems.title: Two unit orientations of the same n-plane differ by a sign (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P and let v, w ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n: continuous linear functionals on n-covectors, ⟨α, v⟩ = v(α)). If v and w are both unit orientations of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf v Q and IsUnitOrientationOf w Q: for some orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P spanning Q, v(α) = ±α(τ) and w(α) = ±α(τ') for all n-covectors α), then w = v or w = −v.

The audited proof of that declaration follows; inside it, 'the parent proof' and 'sibling' refer to that declaration's own original parent node and siblings, not to this decomposition.
Source: the linear-algebra part of step 3 of the parent proof (orthonormal bases of Q differ by an orthogonal matrix of determinant ±1).

1. Unfolding the hypotheses: there are orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q = span(range τ'), and signs ε, ε' ∈ {1, −1} with v(α) = ε·α(τ) and w(α) = ε'·α(τ') for every n-covector α (continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ).

2. Each τ_i and τ'_i lies in Q, so τ, τ' may be regarded as families in the inner product space Q, where they are still orthonormal. Since τ is linearly independent and spans Q, dim Q = n; an orthonormal (hence linearly independent) family of n vectors in the n-dimensional space Q spans Q. Hence τ and τ' are orthonormal bases b and b' of Q indexed by Fin n.

3. Let d := det_b(b'), the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix from b to b'. Both bases are orthonormal, so this matrix is orthogonal and d ∈ {1, −1} (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real).

4. Let α be an n-covector and α_Q its restriction to Q (α composed with the inclusion Q → ℝ^P in each slot), an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q. Every such form is a multiple of det_b: α_Q = α_Q(b)·det_b (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α(τ') = α_Q(b') = α_Q(b)·det_b(b') = d·α(τ). The number d does not depend on α.

5. Hence for every α: w(α) = ε'·α(τ') = ε'd·α(τ) = (εε'd)·(ε·α(τ)) = s·v(α), where s := εε'd ∈ {1, −1} (using ε² = 1). Therefore w = s·v, i.e. w = v if s = 1 and w = −v if s = −1. For n = 0 the same argument applies (τ = τ' is the empty family, Q = {0}, d = 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: Both orthonormal families spanning Q are orthonormal bases b, b' of Q.
det_b(b') = ±1 because the change-of-basis matrix is orthogonal.
For every n-covector α, α(τ') = det_b(b')·α(τ) since alternating n-forms on Q are multiples of det_b.
Therefore w = (εε'det_b(b'))·v with εε'det_b(b') ∈ {±1}.

subproblems.title: A map that is C¹ on an open neighbourhood of a compact set agrees near it with a globally Lipschitz C¹ map
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, K ⊆ ℝ^P compact, O ⊆ ℝ^P open with K ⊆ O, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O; no assumption on f off O). Then there are g : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on all of ℝ^P (ContDiff ℝ 1 g) and L ∈ ℝ≥0 such that g is L-Lipschitz on ℝ^P and, for every x ∈ K, g(x) = f(x) and Dg(x) = Df(x) (fderiv ℝ g x = fderiv ℝ f x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (K O : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsCompact K → IsOpen O → K ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → ∃ (g : Euclid P → Euclid P) (L : NNReal), ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ LipschitzWith L g ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, g x = f x ∧ fderiv ℝ g x = fderiv ℝ f x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1(c) of the parent proof (the cutoff f̂ := χf with χ = 1 near K and tsupport χ inside O; f̂ is C¹ with compactly supported continuous derivative, hence Lipschitz by the mean value inequality, and f̂ = f near K).
Notation: thickening(r, K) := {x : dist(x, K) < r} (open), cthickening(r, K) := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ r} (closed); tsupport χ := closure{χ ≠ 0}.
1. Room around K. K is compact, O is open and K ⊆ O, so there is δ > 0 with cthickening(δ, K) ⊆ O (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put t := cthickening(δ/3, K) (closed) and s := thickening(2δ/3, K) (open). Then t ⊆ s (Mathlib cthickening_subset_thickening', since δ/3 < 2δ/3).
2. Smooth Urysohn function. There is χ : ℝ^P → ℝ of class C^∞ with values in [0, 1], support χ = s, and χ(x) = 1 exactly for x ∈ t (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff for the open set s ⊇ the closed set t). Hence tsupport χ = closure(s) ⊆ cthickening(2δ/3, K) (Mathlib closure_thickening_subset_cthickening) ⊆ cthickening(δ, K) ⊆ O. The set cthickening(2δ/3, K) is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper), so χ has compact support.
3. Definition. g(x) := χ(x)·f(x) for x ∈ ℝ^P. Where χ(x) = 0 (in particular off s, hence off O) we have g(x) = 0 whatever f(x) is.
4. g is C¹ on ℝ^P. It suffices to prove that g is C¹ at every point x (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt). If x ∈ O: O is an open neighbourhood of x on which f is C¹, so f is C¹ at x (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt with O ∈ 𝓝 x); χ is C^∞ at x; so g = χ·f is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.smul). If x ∉ O: then x ∉ tsupport χ (step 2), the complement of the closed set tsupport χ is an open neighbourhood of x on which χ = 0, hence g = 0 on it, and g is C¹ at x (a function eventually equal to the constant 0; ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
5. g = f near K. Let x ∈ K. The open set thickening(δ/3, K) contains x and is contained in t, where χ = 1; so g = f on a neighbourhood of x. Therefore g(x) = f(x), and Dg(x) = Df(x) because Fréchet derivatives only depend on the germ (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
6. Lipschitz bound. g has compact support (it vanishes off tsupport χ; HasCompactSupport.smul_right), hence Dg has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv), and Dg is continuous since g is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). A continuous function with compact support is bounded: there is C with ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ C for all x (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). Let L := max(C, 0) ∈ ℝ≥0. By the mean value inequality on the convex set ℝ^P (lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le, g differentiable everywhere), g is L-Lipschitz. Together with steps 4 and 5 this proves the claim. ∎
Remark: K = ∅ needs no separate treatment (then every δ > 0 works, χ ≡ 0 and g ≡ 0).

subproblems.title: A map with injective derivative on a Borel set is countably piecewise bi-Lipschitz there
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and B ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel such that H is differentiable at every a ∈ B with injective derivative DH(a) (fderiv ℝ H a). Then there are Borel sets C_l ⊆ ℝⁿ (l ∈ ℕ), pairwise disjoint, with ⋃_l C_l = B, and constants m_l > 0 such that m_l·|a − a'| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| for all l and all a, a' ∈ C_l.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (H : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)), MeasurableSet B → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ H a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ H a)) → ∃ (C : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (m : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ l, MeasurableSet (C l)) ∧ Pairwise (fun k l => Disjoint (C k) (C l)) ∧ (⋃ l, C l) = B ∧ (∀ l, 0 < m l) ∧ ∀ l, ∀ a ∈ C l, ∀ a' ∈ C l, m l * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖H a - H a'‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the partition step of the parent proof (step 2(d), reused verbatim in its step 7: Mathlib's partition lemma with the radius r(A) := 1/(2K_A) for injective A, then |H(u) − H(v)| ≥ (2K_A)⁻¹|u − v| on each piece).
1. Coercivity constants. If A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is an injective continuous linear map, then ker A = 0 and, ℝⁿ being finite-dimensional, A is K-antilipschitz for some K > 0 (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith): |v| ≤ K|Av| for all v. Put c(A) := 1/K > 0, so c(A)|v| ≤ |Av| for all v. For non-injective A put c(A) := 1. (The choice of K is made once for each A, by choice.) Define the radius r(A) := c(A)/2, an element of ℝ≥0 with r(A) ≠ 0 for every A.
2. Partition. For a ∈ B, H is differentiable at a, so H has derivative DH(a) at a within B. Apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to f := H, s := B, f' := DH and the radius r of step 1 (r(A) ≠ 0 for all A). It gives Borel sets t_l (l ∈ ℕ), pairwise disjoint, with B ⊆ ⋃_l t_l, and continuous linear maps A_l such that (i) |H(a) − H(a') − A_l(a − a')| ≤ r(A_l)·|a − a'| for all a, a' ∈ B ∩ t_l (ApproximatesLinearOn), and (ii) if B ≠ ∅ then for every l there is y_l ∈ B with A_l = DH(y_l).
3. Pieces. Put C_l := B ∩ t_l and m_l := r(A_l) = c(A_l)/2 > 0. Each C_l is Borel (B and t_l are), the C_l are pairwise disjoint (C_l ⊆ t_l), and ⋃_l C_l = B ∩ ⋃_l t_l = B.
4. Lower bound. Let a, a' ∈ C_l. Then B ≠ ∅, so A_l = DH(y_l) with y_l ∈ B, which is injective by hypothesis; by step 1, c(A_l)|a − a'| ≤ |A_l(a − a')|. By the triangle inequality and (i), |A_l(a − a')| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| + |H(a) − H(a') − A_l(a − a')| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| + (c(A_l)/2)|a − a'|. Hence m_l|a − a'| = (c(A_l)/2)|a − a'| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')|. ∎

subproblems.title: A summable series of integer-weighted Lipschitz parametrized pieces defines an integer multiplicity current
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. For i ∈ ℕ let H_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be Lipschitz, B_i ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel with H_i differentiable at every point of B_i and H_i(B_i) ⊆ U, w_i : ℝⁿ → ℕ measurable, and ζ_i : ℝⁿ → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) a.e. strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure on B_i, such that for a.e. a ∈ B_i there is s ∈ {1, −1} with ζ_i(a)(α) = s·α(DH_i(a)e) for every n-covector α (Ae := (Ae₁, …, Aeₙ)). Write J_i(a) := (det(DH_i(a)*∘DH_i(a)))^{1/2} and assume Σ_i ∫⁻_{B_i} w_i(a)J_i(a) da < ∞. Then there is an integer multiplicity triple R in U (IMRep U n) such that for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the real series Σ_i ∫_{B_i} w_i(a)·ζ_i(a)(ω(H_i(a))) da has sum R.action(ω) (HasSum).

Notation: Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ; I_i(ω) := ∫_{B_i} w_i(a)ζ_i(a)(ω(H_i(a))) da.
1. Good parameters. B_i⁺ := {a ∈ B_i : J_i(a) > 0 and w_i(a) ≥ 1}. J_i is Borel (a ↦ DH_i(a) is Borel by Mathlib measurable_fderiv; A ↦ (det(A*A))^{1/2} is continuous) and w_i is measurable, so B_i⁺ is Borel. For a ∈ B_i⁺, DH_i(a) is injective: det(A*A) > 0 makes the endomorphism A*A of ℝⁿ invertible, and Av = Av' implies A*Av = A*Av', hence v = v'.
2. Partition (parent step 7). Sibling bilip_partition applied to (H_i, B_i⁺) gives pairwise disjoint Borel sets C_{il} (l ∈ ℕ) with ⋃_l C_{il} = B_i⁺ and constants m_{il} > 0 with m_{il}|a − a'| ≤ |H_i(a) − H_i(a')| on C_{il}.
3. Pieces (parent step 8). For each (i, l), sibling piece_imrep applies to (U, H_i, C_{il}, Lipschitz constant of H_i, m_{il}, w_i, ζ_i): C_{il} is Borel; H_i is bi-Lipschitz on C_{il} and differentiable with injective derivative there (C_{il} ⊆ B_i⁺, step 1); H_i(C_{il}) ⊆ H_i(B_i) ⊆ U; w_i is measurable with w_i ≥ 1 on C_{il}; ζ_i is a.e. strongly measurable on C_{il} and has the sign property a.e. on C_{il} (restrictions of the hypotheses on B_i ⊇ C_{il}); and ∫⁻_{C_{il}} w_iJ_i ≤ ∫⁻_{B_i} w_iJ_i < ∞ (a term of a finite series). It gives IMReps R_{il} in U with R_{il}.measure U = ∫⁻_{C_{il}} w_iJ_i and R_{il}.action(ω) = ∫_{C_{il}} w_i(a)ζ_i(a)(ω(H_i(a))) da for every n-form ω.
4. Summation (parent steps 9–11). Let k ↦ (i(k), l(k)) be a bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ (Nat.pairEquiv.symm) and R'_k := R_{i(k)l(k)}. Reindexing and Fubini for nonnegative series (ENNReal.tsum_prod'), and countable additivity of the lower integral over the disjoint Borel sets C_{il} with union B_i⁺ (lintegral_iUnion), give Σ_k R'_k.measure U = Σ_i Σ_l ∫⁻_{C_{il}} w_iJ_i = Σ_i ∫⁻_{B_i⁺} w_iJ_i ≤ Σ_i ∫⁻_{B_i} w_iJ_i < ∞. By sibling imrep_tsum there is an IMRep R in U with HasSum (k ↦ R'_k.action(ω)) (R.action(ω)) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
5. Domination and vanishing. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). It is continuous with compact support, so ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ B_ω for all y (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). For a.e. a ∈ B_i, with s as in the hypothesis, |w_i(a)ζ_i(a)(ω(H_i(a)))| = w_i(a)·|ω(H_i(a))(DH_i(a)e)| ≤ w_i(a)·J_i(a)·B_ω by sibling jac_algebra (b). The integrand is a.e. strongly measurable on B_i (it agrees a.e. with a ↦ w_i(a)·ζ̃_i(a)(ω(H_i(a))) for a strongly measurable ζ̃_i = ζ_i a.e., ω∘H_i being continuous and evaluation being continuous bilinear), and ∫_{B_i} w_iJ_iB_ω < ∞, so the integrand is integrable on B_i. It vanishes a.e. on B_i ∖ B_i⁺: at such a either w_i(a) = 0, or J_i(a) = 0 and then |ω(H_i(a))(DH_i(a)e)| ≤ J_i(a)‖ω(H_i(a))‖ = 0 (jac_algebra (b)), so ζ_i(a)(ω(H_i(a))) = s·0 = 0. Hence I_i(ω) = ∫_{B_i⁺} w_i(a)ζ_i(a)(ω(H_i(a))) da (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero).
6. Identification. For each i, countable additivity of the Bochner integral over the disjoint Borel sets C_{il} with union B_i⁺ (hasSum_integral_iUnion, using the integrability of step 5) and step 3 give HasSum (l ↦ R_{il}.action(ω)) (I_i(ω)). Transporting step 4 through the bijection (Equiv.hasSum_iff), HasSum ((i, l) ↦ R_{il}.action(ω)) (R.action(ω)). Summing fiberwise (HasSum.prod_fiberwise) gives HasSum (i ↦ I_i(ω)) (R.action(ω)), for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎
